title: Agent Interlock Security Statistics
description: Aggregate security statistics reduced from ledger events by joining each tenant_id + interaction_id across its lifecycle (INTERACTION_REQUESTED -> CONTROL_EVALUATED -> ACTION_EXECUTED -> SECURITY_OUTCOME_SET). Events without an interaction_id and groups without INTERACTION_REQUESTED do not participate. Python (agent_interlock.analytics) and the Studio offline importer MUST produce identical values for the same events; the shared golden fixture is schemas/fixtures/analytics-events.json -> analytics-statistics.json.

partitions.description: One entry per data_source present in the events (PRODUCTION / SIMULATION / RED_TEAM / TEST), sorted ascending. Sources are never merged: simulation traffic must not inflate production statistics.

outcomes.description: Interaction count per final securityOutcome (the LAST SECURITY_OUTCOME_SET of each interaction; UNKNOWN when none was set). Keys sorted ascending.

byPolicy.description: Grouped by the policyId of the strongest control decision. Interactions with no CONTROL_EVALUATED event carry no policy and are omitted here (they still count everywhere else).

byMode.description: Grouped by the mode attached to the strongest control decision. Interactions without a control event are omitted.

byReasonCode.description: Interactions touched per reason code, deduped within an interaction. One interaction can carry several reason codes, so the sum over reason codes legitimately EXCEEDS the blocked-interaction count; never treat these as disjoint.

byCheck.description: Coverage per canonical check id, across every enforcement point: which controls were switched on, which looked, and which flagged. Check ids are NOT reason codes -- a check can emit several reason keys and a profile renames them per point, so the join from coverage to byReasonCode must go through the profile's rename map, never a string match. Sorted by checkId. The catalogue is the union of every armed set declared in the stream, so a check nothing declares does not appear at all.

byEdge.description: Grouped by the (sourceActorId, targetActorId, policyId) triple of the strongest control decision, sorted ascending. The pair alone is not a key: the graph permits several edges between one actor pair, and policyId splits precisely where the armed set can differ. Interactions with no complete triple are omitted here and counted in `unattributed`. Studio maps the triple to an edge label from the ArchitectureGraph it already holds.

byCheck.description: The cross-tabulation: on this segment, which controls applied and what happened. Checks ABSENT for EVERY interaction on the edge are omitted to bound the payload -- their absence from this array means ABSENT throughout, which the partition-level byCheck still reports.

unattributed.description: Counters over the interactions that could not be placed on the byEdge grid: no target actor, or no CONTROL_EVALUATED and therefore no policyId. Kept as an explicit bucket rather than dropped, so byEdge sums can be reconciled against the partition total. Detecting traffic on an UNDECLARED edge is a different question and is not answered here -- that belongs to compare_observed_runtime, which holds the declared graph.

timeSeries.description: Hourly UTC buckets of each interaction's FIRST event time, sorted ascending. bucketStart format: YYYY-MM-DDThh:00:00Z.

checkCoverage.description: One canonical check id and the four coverage states, in interactions. RAN_FLAGGED: the check id appears in control.flaggedChecks. RAN_CLEAN: in the declaration's `evaluated` and not flagged. INAPPLICABLE: armed for this link but this invocation gave it nothing to judge. ABSENT: in the catalogue but not armed here -- the operator switched it off, or the enforcement point does not carry it. The four are disjoint and sum to the row's interaction count. This measures COVERAGE, not safety: it can say a control we have did not run, and says nothing about a control we do not have.

counters.description: Interaction-level metrics. decision = strongest_decision over the interaction's CONTROL_EVALUATED control.decision values, ranked BYPASSED < ALLOW < SANITIZE < DEGRADE < CHALLENGE < HOLD < BLOCK < ERROR < QUARANTINE < REVOKE < KILL; unknown strings rank as BLOCK. An execution attempt is an ACTION_EXECUTED with a non-null connectorExecutionId -- the enforcement ACTION_EXECUTED emitted on a block carries connectorExecutionId null and is NOT an attempt.

blockDecisionCount.description: Interactions refused by a control: strongest decision != ALLOW, OR every CONTROL_EVALUATED did not carry control.executionPermitted true (an absent key reads as permitted). A refusal-level metric, regardless of mode: says nothing about whether execution was actually prevented.

shadowWouldBlockCount.description: Refusals (see blockDecisionCount) that were NOT enforced (actualEnforced false, e.g. SHADOW/OBSERVE mode): would have been blocked under ENFORCE.

enforcedBlockCount.description: Refusals (see blockDecisionCount) with actualEnforced true, a completed enforcement ACTION_EXECUTED (null connectorExecutionId), no connector attempt, and final securityOutcome BLOCKED.

executionAttemptCount.description: Interactions where a connector execution was attempted (ACTION_EXECUTED with non-null connectorExecutionId).

executionSuccessCount.description: Interactions with at least one attempted connector execution whose result was COMPLETED.

partialOrBypassCount.description: Interactions whose final securityOutcome is PARTIALLY_EXECUTED, or whose enforced refusal (see blockDecisionCount) was followed by a connector execution attempt anyway (enforcement bypass).

noControlRecordCount.description: Interactions carrying no CONTROL_EVALUATED at all. They reduce to decision ALLOW with an empty reason list, which is shape-identical to a control that ran and allowed, so without this counter a row reading "40 calls, 0 blocked" cannot be told from one where no control ever looked. Reported in every grouping because the blind spot is per-row.
